summary.intent: Conduct a security review of the feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db branch (which adds IPNS signature/pubkey storage in the DB), then implement all identified security fixes and resolve PR review comments.
summary.outcome: All HIGH/MEDIUM security findings were fixed (pubKey-to-ipnsName binding check, web app base64 crash fix, publicKey forwarding on publish, server-side validation), the @cipherbox/crypto package was fixed to build correctly for both CJS (NestJS/Jest) and ESM (Vite/browser) environments, all PR review threads were resolved, and a security review report was committed to .planning/security/.

repo: @cipherbox/crypto depends on ESM-only packages (@libp2p/crypto, @noble/ed25519, @noble/hashes, ipns) which must be bundled into the CJS output via tsup noExternal to work in NestJS and Jest
The NestJS API (apps/api) does not declare @cipherbox/crypto as a dependency — it had to be added to apps/api/package.json before the server-side deriveIpnsName check could be added
The 'Verify API Spec' CI job was missing a build step for @cipherbox/crypto, causing it to fail after the new dependency was added

IPNS names are cryptographically derived from the Ed25519 public key via deriveIpnsName() from @cipherbox/crypto — test fixtures using dummy ipnsNames that don't match the test pubkey will break the new binding validation
The web app resolveIpnsRecord was using spread-based btoa (Array.from + spread) which causes call-stack overflow on large records; the SDK-core had already fixed this but the web service had not
Deferred items for this phase are tracked in .planning/DEFERRED.md

code.finding: Must use split CJS/ESM build configs: CJS with noExternal to bundle all ESM-only deps, ESM with external deps for Vite compatibility. A single config with noExternal breaks Vite browser builds due to Node.js Buffer references.
After Ed25519 signature verification, must derive IPNS name from returned pubKey and compare to requested ipnsName to prevent key substitution attacks by a compromised server

Web app had two bugs: (1) spread-based base64 encoding crashes on large records, (2) publicKey was not forwarded on batch publish, making server-side and client-side pubKey validation dead code for web-published records

Test fixtures used a dummy ipnsName that doesn't derive from the test public key — after adding server-side pubKey-to-ipnsName binding, the correct ipnsName must be derived from the actual test pubKey bytes
MaxLength(100) on publicKey field was inconsistent with actual base64-encoded 32-byte key size (~44 chars); corrected to MaxLength(70)

workflow: Verify the API actually starts locally (not just builds) before pushing to CI — a successful nest build does not guarantee the runtime CJS require chain works

When bundling ESM-only deps into CJS output with tsup, use a separate config entry per format rather than a single config, to avoid the bundled Node.js-specific code (Buffer) breaking Vite browser builds
Security review commits should precede fix commits so the report and fixes have separate, traceable commits
Use 'gh api graphql' for resolving PR review threads; REST replies require integer comment IDs while GraphQL mutations use string thread node IDs

friction: Two rounds of CI failures for the @cipherbox/crypto CJS bundling issue: first attempt (noExternal for specific packages) still left @noble/ed25519 as external; second attempt (noExternal: [/.*/]) broke Vite; required a third split-config approach
1Password SSH signing agent caused intermittent commit failures requiring manual retry
The 'Verify API Spec' CI job had a missing build dependency step that was only discovered after pushing
API startup test had to be done manually (via background process kill) since there's no isolated integration test for module loading
open_items: CodeRabbit thread #5 (deferred): validate signedRecord bytes against the DTO's record field on write in apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:83 — server currently stores whatever signed record bytes the client sends without cross-checking against the record field — tracked in .planning/DEFERRED.md

signatureVerified boolean is returned from resolveIpnsRecord but no caller enforces it — callers proceed even when signature verification is absent/skipped — design decision to leave informational for now
